_about: What people actually say they want, grouped into bubbles, with what each one means in numbers and what plan it implies. Built 2026-09-08 from surveys, search volumes, Google autocomplete and open forums. Every number carries its source key in sources.md. Nothing here is wired into the app.
_how_to_read: Top level = the first bubble a person taps, two or three plain words with a short sub line under it. children = the 'what specifically?' second tap, also short. Never a third tap, and never a word someone would have to stop and work out. aliases = the longer phrasings people really type, kept for matching and for reading back, never on a button. mapsTo = which of our five onboarding goals this lands on, or null when none fits. Limits (injury, health condition, age) are NOT here: see deferred_constraints_screen.

cross_cutting_modifiers._note: These attach to any bubble. They are not goals, they change the numbers or the selection.
cross_cutting_modifiers.deadline: A date (wedding, holiday, race, season). Turns the goal into a rate. Brides: 70% want to lose, want 23 lb, half succeed at ~7 lb.
cross_cutting_modifiers.body_part: Arms, belly, glutes, thighs, chest. Cannot spot-reduce fat; can add volume to a muscle.
cross_cutting_modifiers.age_bracket: Over 40 / 50 / 60 appear in nearly every autocomplete, and were briefly a child of Build muscle. Moved out: an age is context, not an ambition. Same program, slower ramp, see research/02-age.md.
cross_cutting_modifiers.sex_phrasing: 'for women' / 'for men' appear constantly. Program shape does not differ; starting loads and ladder entry do, see research/03-sex.md.
cross_cutting_modifiers.medical_context: PCOS, thyroid, perimenopause, breastfeeding, prediabetes, blood pressure. Same training, refer nutrition and medical. We do not do nutrition.
cross_cutting_modifiers.location: at home / at the gym / without weights / no equipment. Selection only.
cross_cutting_modifiers.fast: 'fast', 'in a week', 'in 2 weeks', 'in 30 days' suffix almost every goal. The app answers the fantasy with the healthy number, never the fantasy.

bubbles.label: Lose weight
bubbles.prevalence: Largest search intent by far: 'how to lose weight fast' ~486k/yr, 'best way to lose weight' 13k/mo. Surveys now rank it below strength, but people search what they will not say. 26-45 year olds' #1 stated reason is 'lose or gain weight' (Mindbody 2019, n=17k). Women 35% vs men 27%.
bubbles.clarifier: How much, or by when, or for what?

children.label: A number of pounds
children.numbers: Safe rate 0.5 to 1% of bodyweight per week, roughly 1 to 2 lb. 20 lb = 10 to 20 weeks. First week or two is mostly water.
children.honest_timeline: Compute the date from the rate and show it. Never accept 'in a month' for 20 lb.
children.plan: 2 to 3 full-body strength days to keep muscle, plus walking or easy cardio, plus steps. Training is maybe 20% of the outcome; the deficit is the rest and we do not do nutrition. Say so.

children.label: Belly fat
aliases: what exercise burns the most belly fat
children.numbers: 'What exercise burns the most belly fat' is 6.4k searches/month. You cannot pick where fat comes off. Belly is usually last for men, hips and thighs for women.
children.honest_timeline: Same as losing a number. The area is where they notice it, not what the plan targets.
children.plan: Identical to 'a number'. Add core strength because they will want it and it does no harm. Do not sell ab exercises as fat loss.

children.label: Before a date
children.numbers: Weeks to date times healthy rate = the honest number. 8 weeks: 2 to 4 kg realistic. 12 weeks: real visible change. Brides: 70% intend to lose, average desired 23 lb, only half lose any, those average ~7 lb, a third gain.
children.honest_timeline: If the ask exceeds weeks x 1% bodyweight, show what IS reachable by that date and offer it. We suggest the healthy rate, never the fastest.
children.plan: Same plan, but the deadline sets the cardio volume and the check-in cadence. The app currently has no concept of a target date.

children.label: For my health
aliases: doctor told me to lose weight
children.numbers: 5 to 10% of bodyweight is the clinically meaningful target: improves blood pressure, HbA1c, lipids (Look AHEAD). 150 min/week moderate activity plus 2 strength days is the standard prescription. 'Prevent future medical issues' is a top-5 stated reason (Mindbody).
children.honest_timeline: 5% of 240 lb is 12 lb, roughly 6 to 12 weeks. Frame the target as 5%, not 'goal weight'.
children.plan: Walking first, 2 strength days, low impact. Prefer machines and supported variants early. This is the safety-led case and it is common.

children.label: The last 10 pounds
children.numbers: Slower by nature: smaller body, lower burn, adaptive thermogenesis. Expect the low end of 0.5%/week.
children.honest_timeline: 10 lb at this stage is 10 to 15 weeks, not 5.
children.plan: Keep or add strength, do not just add cardio. Often better served by the Recomp bubble.

children.label: Lose fat and build muscle
aliases: i want to lose weight and build muscle
workout plan to lose weight and gain muscle
i want to build muscle and lose fat
children.numbers: One of the most common phrasings in autocomplete. Nobody says 'recomp'. This is our Recomp goal in their words.
children.honest_timeline: Route to the Recomp bubble.
children.plan: See recomp.

bubbles.label: Build muscle
bubbles.prevalence: Surveys' #1 stated goal: 'build muscle or strength' 50% (HFA/Kantar, n=2000, both 2025 and 2026). 'How to build muscle' 52.8k/yr, 'how to gain weight' 79k/yr, 'how to get bigger arms' 22.8k/yr. Gen Z 61% more likely than Gen X to lift for aesthetics (Strava).

children.label: Gain weight
children.numbers: Beginner 1 to 1.5% bodyweight per month (~2 lb), intermediate 0.5 to 1%, advanced 0.25 to 0.5%. First year 10 to 15 lb of actual muscle for men. 20 lb of scale weight for a skinny beginner: ~5 months typical, faster with fat.
children.honest_timeline: Muscle is slow. Scale weight is faster because some is fat, water and glycogen. Say which one the number is.
children.plan: 3 to 4 days, 10 to 20 hard sets per muscle per week, mostly 6 to 12 reps, progressive overload, calorie surplus. Surplus is the part we do not control.

children.label: Arms, chest, shoulders
children.numbers: 'Best workout for' autocomplete is almost entirely body parts: abs, glutes, traps, biceps, chest, lower chest, triceps. Arms: beginners can add an inch in 4 to 6 months; roughly an inch per 10 lb of bodyweight gained; natural ceiling 15 to 18 in.
children.honest_timeline: Months, not weeks. Arm growth needs bodyweight growth.
children.plan: Full-body program with 4 to 8 extra weekly sets for the part. Never a part-only program.

children.label: Glutes
children.numbers: The most searched body-part goal among women. Firmer in 4 to 6 weeks, visible size 8 to 12 weeks, significant change 4 to 6 months. Beginner women gain roughly 0.25 to 0.5 kg total muscle per month.
children.honest_timeline: 12 weeks to see it. 6 months to be sure.
children.plan: Hip thrust, RDL, split squat, 2 to 3 times a week, progressive load, eating enough. Inside a full-body plan.

children.label: Skinny fat
children.numbers: Consensus: do not cut. Recomp at maintenance or a small (~10%) surplus, minimum 4 months, then decide.
children.honest_timeline: 6 to 12 months for a real transformation.
children.plan: Route to recomp with a build emphasis.

children.label: Without getting bulky
children.numbers: Women gain about 1 lb of muscle a month as beginners. Relative gains match men; absolute gains are smaller because starting mass is smaller. Bulky does not happen by accident.
children.honest_timeline: Same as overall. The fear is not the timeline.
children.plan: Identical to build-overall. The word 'toned' means this plus a little fat loss.

bubbles.label: Get stronger
bubbles.prevalence: 42.3% say getting physically stronger is their PRIMARY 2026 goal (Life Time, n=750). 46.5% plan to lift more. Strength overtook weight loss in every 2025-26 survey found. 'I want to be strong and fit' is a top-8 reason for both sexes (Mindbody).
bubbles.clarifier: A number on a lift, or strong for life?

children.label: Hit a number
children.numbers: 225 bench: only 17% of men surveyed have ever done it (Outlift, n=585). 1 in 100 in year one, 1 in 20 after a year, 1 in 6 after 3 years, a third after 5. Coaches say 1 to 3 years for most men who train seriously. StrengthLevel (48.7M lifts): 180 lb male beginner ~127, novice 169, intermediate 220; 140 lb female beginner 44, novice 72, intermediate 108.
children.honest_timeline: Compute from their bodyweight and current numbers, not from the ask. A 160 lb man asking for 225 in 6 months should be told 18 to 36 months.
children.plan: 3 to 4 days, the lift twice a week, 3 to 6 reps on main work, linear progression until it stalls. Starting load from bodyweight (allometric) and sex, then logs.

children.label: Lift my bodyweight
children.numbers: OHP 1x, bench 1.5x, squat 2x, deadlift 2.5x are advanced male markers, not year-one targets. Realistic year one: beginner to novice-intermediate on StrengthLevel, +10 to 25% on lifts after the first newbie jump.
children.honest_timeline: Years for the multiples. Months for the first big jump.
children.plan: Same as a-lift.

children.label: Stronger, not bigger
aliases: how to get stronger without getting bigger
children.numbers: A real autocomplete. Heavy low-rep work builds strength with less size than moderate-rep work; some size still comes.
children.honest_timeline: Same as any strength goal.
children.plan: 1 to 5 reps, longer rest, fewer total sets, maintenance calories.

children.label: For everyday life
children.numbers: 'Exercises to strengthen knees' is the #1 autocomplete for 'exercises to'. Grip and leg strength predict mortality; NSCA recommends power work for older adults.
children.honest_timeline: Noticeable in 4 to 8 weeks. This is a forever goal.
children.plan: Compound lifts 2 to 3x, carries, some fast-intent work, balance. Overlaps the feel-better bubble.

children.label: Get back to where I was
aliases: get back to my old numbers
children.numbers: Muscle memory is real: previously trained people regain in roughly a tenth of the original time. After 4+ weeks off, start at ~50% of old loads. 5 weeks of retraining recovered a 10-week break in one study.
children.honest_timeline: Weeks to months, not years. Faster than they fear.
children.plan: Route to the get-back-into-it bubble.

bubbles.label: Tone up
bubbles.prevalence: 'Toned' is the most common word women use for what they want (PureGym, BetterMe, trainer consensus). 'How to get a six pack' 145k/yr, 'how do I get a six-pack' 3.6k/mo. 'Get toned' is a Freeletics onboarding option; 'Muscle Tone' is a Fitbod one. 'Look better physically' is the #1 reason for 18-25s (32.5%, Mindbody).

children.label: Arms, legs, stomach
children.numbers: Every autocomplete for 'how to get toned' is a body part. 'Toned' = enough muscle to have shape + low enough fat to see it. It is recomp with a body-part emphasis.
children.honest_timeline: Feel it in 2 weeks, see it in 4 to 8, others notice at 12.
children.plan: Full-body strength 3x, extra sets for the part, maintenance or small deficit. Same plan as build-a-part with less food.

children.label: Abs
children.numbers: Abs are a body-fat number, not an exercise. Men: outline ~14 to 17%, clear at 10 to 13%. Women: tone ~21 to 24%, clear at 16 to 20%. 'How to get abs in a week / 2 weeks / one day / 5 minutes' are all autocompletes.
children.honest_timeline: From 25% to 12% at 1%/week of bodyweight is roughly 4 to 6 months. Never 30 days.
children.plan: It is the lose-weight plan with core work added for shape. Say the honest body-fat math out loud.

children.label: Get lean
aliases: look good in a bathing suit
workout plan to get lean female
children.numbers: 8 to 12 weeks for a noticeable change; 2 to 4 kg of fat over 8 weeks is realistic. Cut vs bulk thresholds: men above ~15% cut, women above ~25%; between, either.
children.honest_timeline: 12 weeks out is the honest start date. 4 weeks out is a nudge, not a transformation.
children.plan: Strength 3 to 4x to hold muscle, deficit, steps. The date decides the cardio.

bubbles.label: Hit a milestone
bubbles.prevalence: 'I want to be able to' autocomplete: do a pull up, touch my toes, run 5 miles, do a handstand, lift my girlfriend, do the splits. Mastery goals; the kind Precision Nutrition says people stick to. Not one of our five goals.

children.label: First pull-up
aliases: how to do a pull up for women
children.numbers: Programs promise 6 to 12 weeks; real accounts run 3 to 6 months and longer. Entry point on the ladder is a function of bodyweight and sex: a 265 lb beginner and a 140 lb one are not doing the same exercise.
children.honest_timeline: 12 weeks if already fairly strong and light. 6 months is normal. 'In 30 days' is an autocomplete and mostly a lie.
children.plan: Dead hangs, scap pulls, negatives, band or machine assisted, rows, 3x a week, inside a full-body plan. calisthenics.mjs already has the chain.

children.label: Push-ups
aliases: how many push ups should I be able to do
children.numbers: Adult average 12 to 18 in a set; men 15 to 25, women 5 to 15. First full push-up: ~8 weeks staged (wall, incline, knee, full), up to 6 to 12 months for some.
children.honest_timeline: 8 weeks to the first one. Add a rep or two a week after.
children.plan: Ladder 2 to 4x a week, never daily maxes.

children.label: Run a 5K
children.numbers: Couch to 5K: 9 weeks, 3 runs a week, ends at 30 minutes of running. First 5K: 35 to 45 minutes typical. Sub-30 needs 9:39/mile; 6 to 10 more weeks for a beginner. Average race times: men 30s ~27:30, women ~5 to 6 minutes slower.
children.honest_timeline: 9 weeks to finish one. 4 to 5 months to break 30. Sub-25 is a year for most.
children.plan: Run-walk to continuous, 3 runs a week, strength 2x for injury proofing. Deterministic, no generator needed.

children.label: Run faster
children.numbers: Sub-8 from 9 to 10 min: 8 to 12 weeks. From 11 to 12 min: several months. Needs 10 to 15 miles a week of base first.
children.honest_timeline: Depends entirely on the current time. Ask it, or measure it.
children.plan: Easy runs, one interval session, one long run, 4 runs a week.

children.label: Touch my toes
children.numbers: 48% of 2026 resolution-setters want to improve mobility, flexibility or posture (HFA/Kantar). Toe touch: 4 to 8 weeks at 5 to 10 min most days. Splits: months to years. 'Fix my posture' and 'improve my posture' are both autocompletes.
children.honest_timeline: Toes in 6 weeks. Splits, do not promise a date.
children.plan: 5 to 10 minutes daily, hips and thoracic spine, plus strength. Nobody's app has a bubble for this and half of people want it.

children.label: Handstand
children.numbers: Freestanding handstand: 3 to 12 months. Skill work, not strength work.
children.honest_timeline: Months of daily practice.
children.plan: Skill practice 10 to 15 min most days alongside normal training.

bubbles.label: Train for an event
bubbles.prevalence: 'How to train for' autocomplete: half marathon, 5k, marathon, hyrox, ironman, 10k, triathlon, pull ups, spartan race. Gen Z 75% more likely than Gen X to say a race or event is their main motivation (Strava). Hyrox went from 570k to 1.5M participants in one season, ~50/50 men and women. Not one of our five goals.
bubbles.clarifier: Which event, and when is it?

children.label: A race
children.numbers: Half: 12 to 16 weeks, 20 from zero; ACSM says 6 to 12 months from sedentary. Marathon plans people actually choose: 4 runs a week (Strava/Runna). First-half goal is to finish; ~2:20 is a common plan target.
children.honest_timeline: Count back from race day. If there are not enough weeks, say so and offer the shorter race.
children.plan: Periodized run plan plus 2 strength days. The date drives everything; our generator has no concept of a date.

children.label: Hyrox
children.numbers: 8 x 1 km runs with 8 stations. 1.5M participants 2025/26, 2.5M expected 2026, 1,200 US training clubs, near-even sex split. Fastest growing mass-participation fitness event in the world.
children.honest_timeline: 8 to 12 weeks for a trained gym-goer to finish. Longer from scratch.
children.plan: Running base plus sled, rower, wall balls, farmer carries, lunges. A pair can do doubles, which is directly our product.

children.label: Obstacle race
children.numbers: Spartan Sprint: 6 to 8 weeks for an average adult. From nothing: 16 weeks at 3 to 4 sessions. Baseline: run 3 miles, 20 push-ups, ideally 1 pull-up.
children.honest_timeline: Sprint in 2 months if already active.
children.plan: Run 1 to 2x, full-body strength, grip and carries.

children.label: A fitness test
aliases: get in shape for the military
children.numbers: 12 weeks recommended. Typical tests: 1.5 mile run, push-ups, sit-ups, sometimes vertical jump or bench. 'Get in shape for the military' is an autocomplete.
children.honest_timeline: 12 weeks, 3 building to 5 days.
children.plan: Test-specific: run intervals, calisthenics volume, core. Deterministic.

children.label: A workout challenge
children.numbers: Beginner scaled Murph 50 to 70 minutes; fit recreational 45 to 70 full.
children.honest_timeline: 8 weeks of specific prep for a scaled version.
children.plan: Pull-up and push-up ladders, running, volume tolerance.

children.label: A sport or a trip
children.numbers: 'Get in shape for hiking / soccer / basketball' are all autocompletes for 'how to get in shape for'.
children.honest_timeline: 8 to 12 weeks before the season or trip.
children.plan: General strength plus conditioning that matches the sport's demands. Sport skill is theirs.

bubbles.sub: a race, a test, a trip

bubbles.label: Feel better
bubbles.prevalence: 'I want to feel good' is top 3 in every age bracket (Mindbody, n=17k). 'Live a long and healthy life' is #1 for 46-65 (33.9%) and top for men (30%). 61% say their primary motivation is a healthier, longer life (Mindbody 2024). Mental health via activity: 42% (2025), 46% (2026). Longevity: 33 to 38% (Life Time). This is the biggest family in surveys and the smallest in fitness apps.
bubbles.clarifier: What would feeling better look like day to day?

children.label: Mood, stress, sleep
children.numbers: Exercise has medium effects on depression (d ≈ -0.43) and anxiety (d ≈ -0.42) vs usual care (Singh 2023, BJSM umbrella review). For anxiety, shorter and lower intensity works best. For depression, group and supervised settings help more. Aerobic shows the largest effects.
children.honest_timeline: Felt within 2 weeks. That is the fastest-returning goal on this list.
children.plan: Frequency over intensity. Walking counts. Doing it with someone counts extra, which is our product.

children.label: Live longer
aliases: live a long and healthy life
children.numbers: Predicted top trend of 2026 (37.8%). What predicts it: VO2max, grip strength, leg strength, muscle mass. Standard floor: 150 min/week moderate plus 2 strength days. 'Improve my vo2 max' is now a Google autocomplete.
children.honest_timeline: Fitness markers move in 8 to 12 weeks. The payoff is decades.
children.plan: Strength 2 to 3x all patterns, easy cardio most days, one harder cardio session a week, carries and balance. Overlaps strong-for-life.

children.label: More energy
children.numbers: Low cardiorespiratory fitness is the usual cause. Walking first, then incline and stairs. Noticeable in 2 to 4 weeks.
children.honest_timeline: Weeks.
children.plan: Brisk walking building to 150 min, 2 strength days for legs, stairs as the test.

children.label: Doctor's orders
children.numbers: 89% of Americans call regular activity one of the most effective forms of preventive healthcare (HFA). 150 min/week plus 2 strength days. If overweight, 5 to 10% loss is the clinical target.
children.honest_timeline: Markers move in 8 to 12 weeks.
children.plan: Route to lose-for-health if weight is the issue, else longevity.

children.label: Loosen up
children.numbers: 48% of 2026 goal-setters (HFA, n=2000). 30% of Mindbody 2024 respondents motivated by mobility. Desk workers: hip flexors are the usual limiter; 2 to 3 short breaks a day beat one long session; felt within a week.
children.honest_timeline: Feel it in a week, toe-touch in 6, posture is a habit not a finish line.
children.plan: 5 to 10 min daily, hips and upper back, plus strength through full range. Missing from every competitor's goal list.

children.label: Aches and pains
children.numbers: 'Exercises to strengthen knees' and 'strengthen lower back' are the top two autocompletes for 'exercises to'. We hold no injury data at all (research/00).
children.honest_timeline: Acute pain: clinician first. Chronic stiffness: weeks.
children.plan: Glute bridge, bird dog, dead bug, supported squats; swap anything that hurts and remember the swap. This is the per-exercise 'this hurts' feature from open-questions #6.

bubbles.label: Get back into it
bubbles.prevalence: 'Getting back into working out / running / the gym' and 'how to start working out again' are autocompletes. Fitbod cohort: only 10.1% of beginners still training at 12 months, median dropout 19 weeks; 55% of people say they 'fully achieved' last year's fitness resolution (HFA), which means 45% did not and are restarting. Not one of our five goals.
aliases: how to start working out for beginners

children.label: After years off
aliases: get back to my old self
children.numbers: Muscle memory: regain in roughly a tenth of the original time; strength returns in weeks. Start at ~50% of old loads after 4+ weeks off. Soreness will be unusually high from novelty, not load. 2 to 4 week assessment cycles before committing to a program.
children.honest_timeline: Most of it back in 6 to 12 weeks. Faster than they expect.
children.plan: Familiar lifts only, half loads, add 10% a week, then the normal plan. Route from strong-again.

children.label: After a baby
children.numbers: 'How to start working out postpartum' is an autocomplete. Weeks 0 to 6: walking, breathing, pelvic floor. 6 to 12: bodyweight with core engagement, address diastasis. Function before appearance; 'get my body back' is the phrase, restore is the plan.
children.honest_timeline: 3 months to a base. Do not sell the pre-baby body.
children.plan: Core and pelvic floor first, then the standard beginner plan. The lose-weight math applies after, not during, the rebuild.

children.label: Total beginner
aliases: how to start working out for beginners
children.numbers: 'Beginner workout for' autocomplete is dominated by women, women over 50, women over 40, men over 50, men over 40. First 28 days of consistency is the strongest predictor of still training at a year (Fitbod cohort, n=100,709 beginners). 4 shorter sessions beat 3 longer for habit; 5 to 6 days causes burnout.
children.honest_timeline: Feel it at 2 weeks, see it at 4 to 8, hear about it at 12. And the median person quits at week 19.
children.plan: The zero-knowledge plan: 3 full-body days, short, easy loads, scheduled to days. Nothing else matters if week 5 does not happen.

bubbles.label: Stay consistent
bubbles.prevalence: 'Establish a regular exercise routine' 44% (HFA 2025). 'How to stay consistent with working out / in the gym / with weight loss / with adhd' are all autocompletes. Fitbod cohort: 90% of beginners gone by month 12. This is our 'Stay consistent' goal and it may be the most honest thing most people want.
bubbles.clarifier: What usually gets in the way?

children.label: I keep quitting
children.numbers: Weekly goals: 10x more likely to hit them ten weeks running than monthly or yearly (Strava). First 28 days predicts the year (Fitbod). Median dropout week 19. Group and partner training improves adherence; the Köhler effect gives the mechanism (research/06).
children.honest_timeline: Get to week 5. Then week 20. Nothing else.
children.plan: Fewest days they will actually do, scheduled to specific days, short sessions, a partner who sees the week. Optimize for showing up, not for the program.

children.label: Don't know where to start
aliases: what should I do at the gym
children.numbers: The most common beginner state. 'How can I build an exercise plan' and 'how much exercise do I need per week' are top googled questions.
children.honest_timeline: Immediate. Hand them the plan.
children.plan: The zero-knowledge plan. Ask nothing else.

children.label: No time
children.numbers: Frequency drives habit more than duration for beginners; 30-minute sessions 4x a week is a sustainable rhythm. Longer sessions only helped adherence in people who already trained often (Fitbod cohort).
children.honest_timeline: Results at the same pace as anyone else if the sessions happen.
children.plan: 20 to 30 minute full-body, 3 to 4x. Session length is a first-order adherence variable that no generator models.

deferred_constraints_screen._status: LATER, not part of the goal screen. Flagged 2026-09-09.
deferred_constraints_screen._why: A health condition, an injury or an age is not a goal, it is a limit on how the goal gets trained for. Mixing them into 'what do you want?' asks somebody to describe a problem when they came to state an ambition. Different question, different screen, and it comes after the plan exists, never before it.
deferred_constraints_screen._shape: One optional screen, phrased as an offer rather than an interrogation: 'Anything we should know?' with a clear skip. Injuries, conditions, things that hurt, equipment you do not have. Never a required step, never before the plan, and it must be answerable later from Setup.
deferred_constraints_screen._product_rule: Still obeys 'ask the goal, then tell them the plan'. The plan is shown first. This screen only ever makes an existing plan safer.
deferred_constraints_screen._also_solved_by: A per-exercise 'this hurts' swap that is remembered, which turns a safety input into a feature people use anyway. See open-questions #6 and research/07 on recording swaps.

lose-medical-context.label: With a health condition
lose-medical-context.numbers: All appear in Google autocomplete for 'how to lose weight'. Training prescription does not change. Nutrition and medical management do, and are out of scope.
lose-medical-context.honest_timeline: Same rates, often slower in practice. Postpartum: core and pelvic floor first, 6 to 12 weeks before intensity.
lose-medical-context.plan: Standard plan, with a clear line that the training side is what we do and the rest belongs to their clinician.

build-older.label: Over 40
aliases: workout for men over 50 to build muscle
build-older.numbers: In autocomplete for every 'build muscle' and 'workout for' prefix. Older adults gain real muscle and strength; NSCA and ACSM both recommend heavy resistance training.
build-older.plan: Same program. Longer warm-up, smaller load jumps, more recovery days early. See research/02-age.md.

back-after-injury.label: After an injury
back-after-injury.numbers: We hold nothing on injuries. The one input that matters most for safety and we never ask.
back-after-injury.plan: Avoid the movement, swap, remember the swap. Do not build a questionnaire.
